correctness.rationale: The exact bond-percolation objective is M_v(p)=1+2S_v(p)/(n-1), S_v counting connected residual unordered pairs by unique path length. Reimplemented all 18,248 Prüfer-word labeled trees for n=2..7, independently counted the distance coefficient profiles, verified a candidate vertex with nonnegative degree-five Bernstein coefficients of every S_u-S_w; the certificate covers the entire real p interval, not just sampled p. Independently derived all eight spider S_v for arms (1,1,5) and the exact optimizer switch at α²+α³=1. For n>=8, center uniquely wins for small p from unique maximal degree three, but at p=1 center has S_c−S_b=n−7>0; continuity forces failure near one. The finite census proof is exact for n<=7, while all-n construction is symbolic.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Continuous-time transmission paths may induce related edge reachability, so merely naming different models would not exclude implication. Comparing actual objectives and quantifiers reveals no full n<=7 all-parameter theorem or first-eight switch in inspected results.

value.rationale: An exact first-order counterexample and universal cutoff for all smaller finite trees resolve a natural structural optimal-intervention question. The all-n spider proves the threshold is not a tiny one-off instance, and the switch parameter is exact; model assumptions remain narrow and explicit.

limitations: One vertex removed, uniform seed post-removal, independent homogeneous edge transmissibility p in (0,1), finite trees only. Exhaustive finite certificate through n=7 relies on correctness of Prüfer enumeration and independently checked Bernstein encoding.
